subject: food-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A fan oven cooks food mainly by which method of heat transfer?
questions.explain: A fan oven circulates hot air currents around the food, cooking it by convection.

questions.q: In a yeast bread dough, what does the yeast produce to make the dough rise?
options: Carbon dioxide from fermentation of sugar
questions.explain: Yeast ferments sugars and releases carbon dioxide gas, which makes the dough rise.

questions.q: The browning of the surface of bread or toast as starch is exposed to dry heat is called:
questions.explain: Dextrinisation is the browning of starch under dry heat, as seen on toast and baked bread crusts.

questions.q: Dextrinisation is the browning of which substance under dry heat?
questions.explain: Dextrinisation is the breakdown and browning of starch when exposed to dry heat, as in toasting bread.

questions.q: The thickening of a sauce when starch granules absorb liquid and swell on heating is called:
questions.explain: Gelatinisation is when starch granules absorb liquid, swell and burst on heating to thicken a sauce.

questions.q: Egg yolk helps oil and vinegar stay mixed in mayonnaise because lecithin acts as an:
questions.explain: Lecithin in egg yolk is an emulsifier that holds oil and water-based liquids together so they do not separate.

questions.q: Which of the following is a biological raising agent?
questions.explain: Yeast is a biological raising agent that produces carbon dioxide through fermentation to make dough rise.

questions.q: Grilling and toasting cook food mainly by which method of heat transfer?
questions.explain: Grilling cooks food by radiation, where heat waves travel directly from the heat source to the food.

questions.q: Whisking egg whites traps air to form a foam. This functional property is known as:
questions.explain: Aeration is the incorporation of air, such as whisking egg whites to make a meringue foam.

questions.q: A starch-thickened sauce left to cool may set firmly into a wobbly mass. This setting on cooling is called:
questions.explain: On cooling, the gelatinised starch sets into a gel, a process known as gelation.

questions.q: Which raising agent works mechanically rather than by a chemical reaction or fermentation?
options: Trapped air from whisking or folding
questions.explain: Trapped air from whisking, folding, sieving or creaming is a mechanical raising agent.

questions.q: Rubbing fat into flour coats the flour particles, which helps to produce a crumbly texture. This property of fat is called:
questions.explain: Shortening is when fat coats flour particles, preventing gluten development and giving a crumbly, short texture.

questions.q: Why does whisking egg white before adding it to a mixture help a cake to rise?
options: It traps air which expands on heating
questions.explain: Whisking aerates the egg white, trapping air bubbles that expand when heated to raise the mixture.

questions.q: When an egg is heated and sets from a runny liquid to a firm solid, this change is called:
questions.explain: Heat causes egg proteins to denature and then coagulate, setting them into a solid.

questions.q: Caramelisation is the browning that occurs when which ingredient is heated to a high temperature?
questions.explain: Caramelisation is the browning and flavour change that happens when sugar is heated to a high temperature.

questions.q: In a roux-based white sauce, what is the main role of the flour?
options: To thicken the sauce through gelatinisation
questions.explain: The starch in flour gelatinises when heated with liquid, thickening the sauce.

questions.q: A cut apple turns brown when left in air. This is an example of:
questions.explain: Enzymic browning happens when enzymes in cut fruit react with oxygen in the air, turning the surface brown.

questions.q: Overcooking green vegetables in lots of water for a long time mainly causes the loss of which nutrient?
questions.explain: Vitamin C is water-soluble and heat-sensitive, so prolonged boiling destroys and leaches it away.

questions.q: Which method of heat transfer occurs by direct contact, such as a pan heating food on a hob?
questions.explain: Conduction transfers heat through direct contact between a heat source, the pan and the food.

questions.q: When self-raising flour is used, the raising agent releases which gas to make a cake rise?
questions.explain: Baking powder in self-raising flour produces carbon dioxide gas, which expands and raises the mixture.

questions.q: Heat transferred through the movement of currents in a liquid or gas is called:
questions.explain: Convection transfers heat by the circulation of currents in liquids or gases, as in boiling water or an oven.

questions.q: When meat is fried at high temperature it browns and develops a savoury flavour. This is mainly due to:
questions.explain: The Maillard reaction is a browning reaction between proteins (amino acids) and sugars under dry heat.
